DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 15 s. 2021 3 February 2021 HON. CANDELARIA V. CALABIA Sangguniang Bayan Member Chairman, Committee on Legal Matters Municipality of Alaminos, Laguna Dear Hon. Calabia: This has reference to your letter dated 27 January 2020, requesting for this Department's legal opinion on the following matters: 1. Is the proposed ordinance legally permissible, or is it violative of the national law, therefore ultra vires or beyond the powers of the Sangguniang Bayan to enact? 2. Is the proposed ordinance which imposes responsibility upon the Municipal Mayor and Sangguniang Bayan to establish a municipal-owned sanitary landfill in accordance with Republic Act No. 9003, which states that the responsibility relative to solid waste management is upon the Municipal Solid Waste Management Board? 3. Does the local initiative proposing to enact the aforesaid ordinance, without the recommendation of the MSWMB, encroaches upon the authority of the latter? 4. Does the proposed ordinance violates Section 44 of RA 9003 in relation to Section 33 of the Local Government Code, and Section 12(9) of RA 9003, with respect to the exclusivity of the sanitary landfill only to the Municipality of Alaminos to the exclusion of other local government units? 5. "Clearly it is not against the declared national policy on solid waste management that encourages inter LGU cooperation and the DENR as well as DILG declared policy of clustering of LGUs with no financial resource to establish by itself a sanitary landfill?

The Municipality of Alaminos "exports" its trash/garbage to the City of San Pedro Laguna as Pilotage is accommodating us to dump in its SLF. Will this declaration that Alaminos does not want garbage from other municipalities be misconstrued as an overly myopic, selfish and isolationist policy and does nor engender good relationship with other LGUs?" (quoted from the letter dated 27 January 2020). Per your representation, on 14 January 2020, the Sangguniang Bayan of Alaminos received a petition from the people, through local initiative, to enact an ordinance, entitled: "Waste Management Ordinance of 2020', otherwise known as the "Executive Sanitary Landfill for Alaminos, Laguna". In effect, the aforesaid ordinance aims to exclusively receive, accept and process wastes from its barangays and within its jurisdiction, to the exclusion of other cities, municipalities and barangays. Hence, the above-mentioned queries. Foremost, Local Initiative is the legal process whereby the registered voters of a local government unit may directly propose, enact, or amend any ordinancel. It shall extend only to subjects or matters which are within the legal powers of the Sanggunian to enact2. With respect to the first issue, we answer in the affirmative. One of the basic services that every municipality should provide, pursuant to Section 17 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), is the establishment of solid waste disposal system or environmental management system and services or facilities related to general hygiene and sanitation3. In relation thereto, the Sangguniang Bayan shall enact an ordinance which provides for an efficient and effective system of solid waste and garbage collection disposal and prohibit littering and placing or throwing of garbage, refuse, and other filth and wastes4. 1 Section 120, RA No. 7160 2 Section 124(b), RA 7160 3 Section RA 7160 Section LGC

Applying the foregoing, the law itself provides that the Sangguniang Bayan is responsible for enacting an ordinance relative to waste disposal, hence, within its powers and authority. Clearly, therefore, the proposed ordinance can be consequently and validly adopted, provided the requisites and requirements provided in RA 7160 and other pertinent laws with respect to local initiative are complied with. On the second issue, however, we answer in the negative. To begin with, it is a basic statutory construction that every statute must be so construed and harmonized with other statutes as to form a uniform system of law, following the legal maxim interpretare et concordare leges legibus est optimus interpretendi modus. Thus, the powers and functions of Municipal Solid Waste Management Board (MSWMB) vis-å-vis power of the Sangguniang Bayan to enact ordinances related to environmental protection and preservation, can be interpreted as follows: Section 12 of Republic Act No. (RA) 9003 in relation to Sections 2 and 3, Rule VII, Part Ill of its Implementing Rules and Regulations, pertains to the creation of MSWMB that is tasked to develop a solid waste management plan. In preparing the said plan, it should reflect, among others, the illustration or map of the city/municipality, indicating the dump sites, landfills and other solid waste facilities, as well as the inventory of existing waste disposal and other solid waste facilities. On the other hand, the LGC states that the municipality, through its Sanggunian, has the power and within its authority to develop, establish and/or enact an ordinance relative to sanitary landfills and other environmental efforts which will thereafter be considered and consolidated by the MSWMB in the preparation of its Municipal Solid Waste Management Plan. Accordingly, despite the presence or absence of ordinance related to sanitary landfills, such fact shall be considered by the MSWMB in its solid waste management plan. Nevertheless, the proposed ordinance should take into consideration Sections 40, 41 and 42 of RA 9003 in relation to Section 1 and 2, Rule XIV of the IRR of RA 9003, with respect to the criteria for establishing and operating sanitary landfills.

Relative to the preceding discussions, we answer the third issue in the negative. Corollarily, there is no need to secure a prior recommendation from MSWMB before the enactment, adoption, and/or issuance of the proposed ordinance. To reiterate, the concerned local government unit has the authority granted by RA 7160 to propose, enact, and develop ordinances and policies related to environmental protection. In line with this, every local government units is mandated under Section 16 of the LGC to promote the health and safety and enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology. With respect to the fourth issue, we answer in the negative. Notably, Section 44 of RA 9003 in relation to Section 5, Rule VII, Part Ill of its IRR, pertains to areas which have common solid waste management problems. This finds application only if the LGUs present commonality with respect to addressing their solid waste management problems. In connection thereto, their respective efforts, services and resources shall likewise be consolidated. It is the duty of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the National Solid Waste Management Commission (NSWMC) to publish guidelines for the identification of areas which have common solid waste management problems, and recommend to the LGUs to consolidate their efforts to jointly address their solid waste management issues, respectively. On the other hand, Section 33 of RA 7160 provides the enactment of an ordinance which embodies the decision of the concemed LGUs to consolidate their efforts for purposes commonly beneficial to them, which in this case, pertains to their solid waste management issues. However, we are constrained not to provide a definite answer to the fifth question as the same is beyond our competence and jurisdiction to decipher and determine. In sum, the ordinance proposed by the people through local initiative, which imposes upon the Municipal Mayor through its sanggunian, the responsibility of establishing and operating a sanitary landfill, is valid. Provided however, that the requirements in Sections 121 to 125 of RA 7160 are complied with.

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, By uthority of the Secretary: OIC-Un e INGAN, CESO Ill ary for Local Government Legal/91 Copy Furnished: DIRECTOR ARIEL O. IGLESIA Regional Director, DILG-CALABARZON 3/F Andenson Bldg. 1 , National Highway Brgy. Parian, Calamba City, Laguna
